decisions.quote:
Although none of the SNPs showed a statistically
          signiﬁcant association with trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity, we show that three (rs8032978, rs7406710
          and rs9316695) and four (rs8032978, rs7406710, rs28415722 and rs11932853) SNPs had an eﬀect in the same
          direction in the Japanese and the Singaporean cohort, respectively, as that in our previous study. Combining
          the previous study with the current replication studies, we ﬁnd a strong association for two SNPs, rs8032978
          and rs7406710, with trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity (Pcombined = 4.92 × 10−5 and 5.50 × 10−5, respectively).
decisions.reason: Addressing the parent scope objection directly: in the two new independent cohorts (Replication 1 and Replication 2), none of the five tested SNPs reached statistical significance (all uncorrected p >= 0.229 against a Bonferroni threshold of p = 0.01), and the Discussion explicitly refers to the unpooled independent-cohort results as 'the replication failure' (supporting 'failed'). However, the authors also emphasize that two of the five SNPs (rs8032978 and rs7406710) showed consistent same-direction effects in both cohorts and strong associations when pooling the new replication cohorts with the original GWAS counts (Pcombined = 4.92 x 10^-5 and 5.50 x 10^-5), concluding in the final paragraph that 'our replication studies using Japanese and Singaporean cohorts supports the potential association of two SNPs with trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity' (supporting 'mixed'). Because the strong statistical support behind the authors' conclusion combines the original discovery data with the new cohorts while the Discussion characterizes the independent-cohort test itself as a replication failure, the scope of the overall conclusion versus the new-data replication test is unresolved by the source text and must remain undeterminable.

decisions.quote:
To validate this association,
          here we performed replication studies using Japanese and Singaporean case-control cohorts (Japan: 6 cases
          and 206 controls; Singapore: 22 cases and 178 controls).
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding agree that the paper is a replication study that collects and genotypes two new independent case-control cohorts (Japanese and Singaporean) to re-test the five SNP associations from the authors' prior GWAS. Addressing the prior quote failure, the quote preserves exact line breaks and whitespace without crossing a hyphenated word break.
